bugs.summary: Visibility differences between bytecode and interpreted evaluation for [ and [[
bugs.creator: ikrylov

comments.text:
As pointed out by Luke Tierney in the [R-devel thread](https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-devel/2024-October/083686.html), while the `[` and `[[` primitive operations force visibility of their results, their bytecode evaluation counterparts do not:

```
x <- structure(1, class = "foo")
`[[.foo` <- `[.foo` <- function(x, i) invisible(2)

withVisible(x[1])
## $value
## [1] 2
## 
## $visible
## [1] TRUE

withVisible(eval(compiler::compile(quote(x[1]))))
## $value
## [1] 2

## $visible
## [1] FALSE

withVisible(x[[1]])
## $value
## [1] 2

## $visible
## [1] TRUE

withVisible(eval(compiler::compile(quote(x[[1]]))))
## $value
## [1] 2

## $visible
## [1] FALSE
```

This discrepancy is not present for `$`, because the `OP(DOLLAR, 2)` branch of `bcEval_loop` sets `R_Visible = TRUE` before continuing. The `@` operator is handled via `OP(CALLSPECIAL, 1)`, which checks the `eval` flag of the primitive operation, so there is no discrepancy there either.

I think that the current code for `OP(STARTSUBSET, 2)` and `OP(STARTSUBSET2, 2)` could take the `eval` flag into account by letting `tryDispatch` access `PRIMPRINT(op)`:

```
Index: src/main/eval.c
===================================================================
--- src/main/eval.c	(revision 87265)
+++ src/main/eval.c	(working copy)
@@ -6047,10 +6047,12 @@
   SEXP pargs, rho1;
   int dispatched = FALSE;
   SEXP op = SYMVALUE(install(generic)); /**** avoid this */
+  int flag = PRIMPRINT(op);
 
   PROTECT(pargs = promiseArgs(CDR(call), rho));
   IF_PROMSXP_SET_PRVALUE(CAR(pargs), x);
 
+  R_Visible = flag != 1;
   /**** Minimal hack to try to handle the S4 case.  If we do the check
 	and do not dispatch then some arguments beyond the first might
 	have been evaluated; these will then be evaluated again by the
@@ -6077,6 +6079,7 @@
 #else
   if (! dispatched) DECREMENT_REFCNT(x);
 #endif
+  if (flag < 2) R_Visible = flag != 1;
   return dispatched;
 }
 
```

This seems to work for the `[` and `[[` S3 methods above and passes `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 make check-devel`, but I am not confident that this covers all possible cases, so not attaching as a suggested patch.
comments.creator: ikrylov
